# Packet — popol-vuh-013: Xquic comes to the grandmother and the net of maize (fols. 17r–18r)

The established text (pinned) follows, one paragraph per block. A unit's `t` is cut from it by script (a sentence, or a long sentence or litany cut at a syntactic joint; couplets never split).

¶1
Arecut e ꜭo ri vchuch Hunbaꜩ, Hunchouen, ta xul ri ixoc Xquic vbi. Ta xul cut ri ixoc Xquic ruꜭ ri vchuch Hunbaꜩ, Hunchouen; xꜭol oc ral chupam, xa zcaquin chic maui que yaqueic ri Hunahpu, Xbalanque qui bi.

¶2
Ta xul curi ixoc chire ri atit; xꜭha curi ixoc chire ri atit: “Mi xin vlic, lal chichu; in alib la, in puch alcual la, lal chichu,” xꜭha, ta xoc vloc ruꜭ ri atit.

¶3
“Apa cat pe vi vloc? Ꜭo chi pa ri val? Ma pa xe camic chi Xibalba? E cu caib canoc quetal, qui ꜩihel puch, Hunbaꜩ, Hunchouen qui bi; ve a vila? Cat pe vi, cat el vbic!” xuꜭhax ri capoh rumal atit.

¶4
“Xere la, quiꜩih vi chi in alib la; xꜭo nare. In ꜭo vi rech Hunhunahpu. Va vcaam e ꜭazlic; maui e caminac ri Hunhunahpu, Vvcub Hunahpu; xa vcatbal rib zac mi xqui bano. Lal valib. Quehe cut i vila ta chi loc vvach ri vcaam,” xuꜭhaxic ri atit.

¶5
Arecut que cacal ri Hunbaꜩ, Hunchouen: xa zu, xa bix ca qui bano, xa zibanic, xa pu cotonic qui chaquih chi hutaquih; arecut cubul vi vꜭux ri atit.

¶6
Xꜭha chicut atit: “Xma ca uah vi at ta valib; xa a hoxbal ri ꜭo cha pam; at ꜭaxtoꜭ. Xe cam vi val ca biyh.”

¶7
Xꜭha chicut ri atit: “Quiꜩih ibare va ca nu biyh. Vꜩ bala, at valib ca nu tao. Vhat bala, ha cama quecha vi chi qui veeh; ha hacha hun chi nima cat; chi petic, at na cu valib ca nu tao,” xuꜭhax cut ri capoh.

¶8
“Vꜩ bala,” xꜭha cut. Catepuch ta xbec pa abix ꜭo vi cabix ri Hunbaꜩ, Hunchouen, hocam vbeel cumal. Xu taqueh cut capoh, xopon puch chi ri pa abix.

¶9
Xa cu huvi ri abix; xma ꜭo chivi vcavi, roxvi; xu vachelaam vi vvach chi huvi. Ta xquiz cut vꜭux ri capoh: “Quila in macol, in ꜭazbol! Apa xchin cam vi ri hun cat echa ca bixic?” xcha cut.

¶10
Catepuch vziquixic Chahal Echa rumal: “Ta hul val oc, ta hul tacal oc. Xtoh, Xcanil, Xcacau, ix pu ꜩiya; at Chahal re queꜭha Hunbaꜩ, Hunchouen!” xꜭha ri capoh.

¶11
Ta xu cam cut ri zamiy, vzamiyal vvi hal; xu boc acan oc; maui xu hach ri hal; chi cau cut ri hal echa pa cat; xcaxinic ri nima cat.

¶12
Ta xpe cut ri capoh. Xa cu chicop xecan ri cat. Ta xpetic, xbe qui ya vcoc xucut ha, quehe ri recan. Xoponic, xril ri atit. Catepuch ta xril ri atit ri echa hun chi nima cat:

¶13
“Apa mi xpe vi ri echa auumal? Mi xe a calaba vi, ve mi xquiz a cam vloc ri cabix? Chi be na vila,” xꜭha ri atit. Ta xbe puch, xbe rila ri abix.

¶14
Xavi xere ꜭo vi ri huvi abix; xavi cu xere calah vcolibal cat chuxe. Anim chicut xpe ri atit, xul chicut chi rochoch; xꜭha chicut chire ri capoh: “Xere vi retal ri quiꜩih vi chi at valib. Chi vil chi na a banoh, ri e ꜭo ri vi e nauinac chic,” xuꜭhax cut capoh.

## Establishment log (doubtful readings, letters chosen, supralinear words — the notes must say so)

# Establishment log — popol-vuh-013 (image 0043 from line 30, 0044, 0045 to line 8)

Read 2026-11-26 from source/pages/i0043 (from l.30, after `… xe moyvachixic conohel.`), all of i0044, and i0045
lines 1–8, in strips of about six lines at 0.9–0.95×, with 1.3–4× crops of every doubtful word, checked word by
word against Brasseur 1861 (OCR lines 23160–23200, 23248–23262, 23344–23366).
Start: `Arecut e ꜭo ri vchuch Hunbaꜩ, Hunchouen …` (0043 l.30, Ximénez's indented paragraph). End: `… xuꜭhax cut
capoh.` (0045 l.8).

**The part ends sooner than planned, at Ximénez's own heading**: 0045 l.9–10 is an indented heading, `Are chic
xchica ꜩihoh calaxic / hunahpu xbalanque` ('Now we shall tell of the birth of Hunahpu and Xbalanque'), followed at
l.11 by a new indented paragraph `Arecut calaxic vae xchica byih …`. 012 began at such a heading (`Va chi cute
vꜩihoxic hun capoh`), and the conventions cut at the manuscript's headings. Running on to the next break (the end
of the monkey episode, 0047 l.~36, before `Catepuch xebixanic`) would have made a part of over four pages.
popol-vuh-014 should begin at **0045 l.9, the heading `Are chic xchi ca ꜩihoh calaxic Hunahpu, Xbalanque`**, and
can run to the end of the transformation of Hunbaꜩ and Hunchouen into monkeys (0047, before the paragraph
`Catepuch xebixanic, xezuanic …`, where the grandmother's four trials begin; Brasseur's chapter runs on through
them to `… ruq pu qui chuch.`).

parts.json: popol-vuh-013 images set to 0043–0045 (last_image 45) and popol-vuh-014 to 0045–0047 (first_image 45,
cite `LoC images 0045–0047`), as 011's and 012's runs did.

Content: Xquic comes to the mother of Hunbaꜩ and Hunchouen (Xmucane), with Hunahpu and Xbalanque in her womb, and
calls herself her daughter-in-law; the old woman refuses her (where are my sons? are they not dead in Xibalba?);
Xquic says Hunhunahpu and Vvcub Hunahpu are alive, what she carries is theirs; Hunbaꜩ and Hunchouen only play the
flute, sing, paint and carve, the old woman's comfort; the old woman calls her a wanton and a deceiver, then sets
her a test: bring a full net of food from the field of Hunbaꜩ and Hunchouen; there is only one plant; Xquic calls
on the guardian of food and Xtoh, Xcanil, Xcacau, pulls the silk of the one ear and fills the net; animals carry
it; the old woman goes to the field, finds the one plant still standing and the print of the net beneath it, and
accepts her: "this is the sign that you are truly my daughter-in-law".

## Folios
Counting as 004–012 did (0043 = 17r): 0044 = 17v, 0045 = 18r → `fols. 17r–18r`. The crop of 0044 carries `17` at
the top left, and 0046 `18` (the folio doubt in QUESTIONS.md, 2026-11-24, again); the earlier count is kept.

## Paragraphs
Ximénez indents only `Arecut e ꜭo` (0043 l.30) in this stretch; the further paragraphs are cut at speech turns and
episode joints, as 011 and 012 did.

## Letter rule used (002–012's rules, unchanged)
- g-shaped → ꜭ: `e ꜭo ri vchuch` (MS `egori`), `ruꜭ` ×2 (MS `rug`), `xꜭol oc` (MS `xgoloc`, B. x-qol-oc),
  `Ꜭo chi pa ri val` (B. qo), `xꜭo nare`, `In ꜭo vi` (B. qo), `e ꜭazlic` (MS `egaz|lic`, B. qazlic), `ri ꜭo cha pam`
  (B. qo ch'a pam), `ꜭaxtoꜭ` (MS `gaxtog`, both letters g-shaped at 3×; B. OCR garbled `Заро`), `ꜭo vi cabix`,
  `xma ꜭo chivi`, `in ꜭazbol` (B. qazbol), `ꜭo vi ri huvi abix` (0045 l.1), `ri e ꜭo ri vi` (0045 l.7).
- gh → ꜭh: `xꜭha` (all but one), `xuꜭhax` ×3, `xuꜭhaxic`; and **`queꜭha Hunbaꜩ`** (0044 l.33, MS `quegha`), where
  0044 l.16 has `quecha` with plain ch for the same word ('their food', B. qu'echa both times) — both as written,
  as 012's `ahuꜭhan` / `ahuchan`.
- plain ch once in the speech tag: **`xcha cut`** (0044 l.29, MS `xcha cut`, every other tag `xgha`) — as written,
  as 006's `cha cut` / `xcha vloc`.
- q-shaped `qux` → `ꜭux` (009's rule): `vꜭux` ×2.
- tz ligature (with its ascender) → ꜩ: `Hunbaꜩ` ×6, `qui ꜩihel`, `quiꜩih` ×3, `Vꜩ bala` ×2, `ix pu ꜩiya`.
- **plain z (ʒ, no ascender) kept as z**, compared at 2–3× with the ligature in `quiꜩihel` (0043 l.43): `xa zcaquin`
  (B. zcaquin), `xa zu`, **`xa zibanic`** (0044 l.8; B. tzibanic; as 012's `vzibel`), `zac`, `xquiz` ×2 (B. qiz),
  **`ri zamiy, vzamiyal`** (0044 l.35; B. tzamiy, u tzamiyal).
- plain c kept where Brasseur has g, q or k: `vcatbal rib` (B. u gatbal), `que cacal` (B. cakal), `cotonic`
  (B. qotonic), `cat` 'net' throughout (B. cat), `capoh` throughout (B. gapoh), `Xcanil` (MS plain c; B. Xganil in
  the K'iche', Xcanil in his French), `xecan` (B. x-ekan), `recan` (B. r'ekan), `vcoc` (B. u coc), `calah`,
  `vcolibal` (B. u qolibal), `ri cabix` (B. k'abix), `xe a calaba` (B. galaba; see below), `Catepuch` ×3 (B. Qate…).

## Names and spellings
- **Hunchouen**: the medial letter is a v-shape at 0043 l.31 and l.33 (`hunchoven`) and looks more like u at 0044
  l.7; Ximénez's medial u and v are hardly distinct here. Printed `Hunchouen` throughout, as 009–012 printed it.
- `Hunhunahpu` ×2 (0044 l.1–2, MS `hunhun ahpu`, `hun hunahpu`), `Vvcub Hunahpu`, `Xquic` ×2, `Xibalba`.
- `Chahal Echa` (0044 l.30) and `Chahal` (l.33) capitalised as the name of the guardian of food invoked by Xquic
  (B. 'Gardien des aliments'); `Xtoh, Xcanil, Xcacau` capitalised as names (B. Xtoh, Xganil, Xcacou).
- Ximénez's word-final `ll` (`rall`, `vall`, `lall`, 0043) printed `l`, as earlier parts printed `ral`, `val`, `lal`.

## Doubtful readings and decisions against Brasseur
- 0043 l.31–32 `ta xul ri ixoc Xquic vbi. Ta xul cut ri ixoc Xquic ruꜭ ri vchuch …`: Brasseur skips from the
  first `ixok Xquiq` to `ruq ri u chuch` (omitting `vbi. Ta xul cut ri ixoc Xquic`); the MS has both clauses,
  printed.
- 0043 l.34 `xꜭol oc ral chupam` (MS one word `xgoloc`): divided with Brasseur.
- 0043 l.44 `ve a vila` (MS `ve avila`; B. `ve ауа?` OCR). Divided by us.
- 0043 l.45 `Cat pe vi, cat el vbic!` (MS `catpevi` + a small z-shaped mark raised after `vi`, then `catelvbic`;
  B. `C'at pe-vi, edis el ubic`): the raised mark is taken as a pause mark, not a letter; `cat el vbic` divided
  with Brasseur's `el ubic`. Doubtful.
- 0043 l.46–47 `Xere la, quiꜩih vi chi in alib la; xꜭo nare` (MS `xerela quiꜩih | vi chi in alibla xgo nare`;
  B. `Xerela quitzih vi chi in alib La x-qo nare`): `nare` left undivided. Doubtful division.
- 0044 l.5 `i vila` (MS `ivila`; B. `yv'ila`), `ta chi loc vvach` (B. `ta chi log m vach`): MS c.
- 0044 l.7 `que cacal`: a letter written over the final l (or a blot); read with Brasseur (cakal).
- 0044 l.11 `Xma ca uah vi at ta valib` (MS `xmacauahvi at ta`; B. `X-ma ca v'ah-vi at-ta`): u as written.
- 0044 l.12 `ri ꜭo cha pam` (MS `rigo chapam`): divided as 012's `co cha pam`.
- 0044 l.13 `at ꜭaxtoꜭ` (B. OCR unreadable): both g-shaped letters clear at 3×; presumably 'deceiver'. Then `xe cam
  vi val` with a blot over `vi` (read with Brasseur `x-e Cam vi v'al`). `ca biyh` ends the line; the next line
  begins `xꜭha chicut ri atit`, set here as the tag introducing her second speech (`Quiꜩih ibare …`), which is hers
  (it ends `xuꜭhax cut ri capoh`). The first speech also opens with a tag (`Xꜭha chicut atit:`).
- 0044 l.16–17 `ha cama quecha vi chi qui veeh; ha hacha` (MS `hacama quecha | vi chiqui veeh hahacha`;
  B. `h'a qama qu'echa vichi qui veeh, h'a hacha`). `veeh` as written. Divided by us.
- 0044 l.21 `ꜭo vi` with a blot over `vi`.
- 0044 l.24–26 `huvi` ×2 (each with a raised t-like mark over the `vi`, taken as Ximénez's heavy accent, which he puts
  on most final `vi` here), `vcavi, roxvi` as written (B. u ca-vi r'ox-vi), `xu vachelaam vi vvach chi huvi`
  (B. `xu vachelaam viu vach chi havi`): MS u in `huvi`.
- 0044 l.30 `Chahal`: a blot over the final l (read with Brasseur).
- 0044 l.31 **`Ta hul val oc, ta hul tacal oc`** (MS `tahul vatloc tahul tacaloc`; B. `ta ul va шос, ta Ful
  takal-oc`): at 4× the stroke after `va` is a tall crossed stroke followed by l, read as Ximénez's crossed l
  doubled (as his `rall`, `vall`), so `val oc`, parallel to `tacal oc`. Doubtful; it may be `va vloc` (Brasseur).
- 0044 l.37 `chi cau cut` (B. chi cau): MS u (bottom-joined), not n.
- 0044 l.38 a struck letter with a blot before `cat` at the line start: not printed.
- 0044 l.41 `xbe qui ya vcoc xucut ha` (MS `xucutha`; B. `xucut ha`).
- 0044 l.45 **`auumal`** (MS `a u u mal`, three minim groups before m; B. aumal): printed as written, one word.
  Doubtful.
- 0044 l.45 **`xe a calaba`** (MS `xe a` + a tall l-like stroke + `calaba`; B. `xe a galaba`): the stroke is not
  the tresillo's 3-shape; taken as a false start and not printed; the c printed plain. Doubtful (Brasseur's g
  would make it ꜫalaba).
- 0045 l.1 `xbe rila` (MS r shaped like v; B. x-be r'ila).
- 0045 l.4 `chi rochoch` (MS `chirochoch`).
- 0045 l.7 **`ri e ꜭo ri vi e nauinac chic`** (MS `riegorivi enauinac | chic`; B. `ri e qo ri vienauinakchie`):
  divided with Brasseur; the sense of `ri vi` is unclear. Doubtful.
- Quotations: the grandmother's two speeches at 0044 l.10–19 are set as two quotations, each with its tag.
